correctness.rationale: The external Theorem 4.8 gives eight exhaustive equations under exact hypotheses. For five rational-base Artin--Schreier covers the pole counts are 2,1,4,5,3, and the classical Deuring--Shafarevich formula gives ranks 2,0,6,8,8. For the other three, explicit birational reductions exhibit the tame bases as elliptic \(v^2=u^3-u\) in characteristic three, elliptic \(v^2=u^3-1\) in characteristic five, and genus-two \(v^2=u^5-1\) in characteristic three. Their Hasse invariants vanish in the elliptic cases; the genus-two Hasse--Witt matrix is nilpotent with square zero; all base p-ranks vanish. The AS function has one pole on each tame base; Deuring--Shafarevich then yields rank zero. A standalone exact checker independently verifies polynomial identities, Hasse coefficients and all eight arithmetic rows. The proof does not infer infinite generality from finite tests. It assumes, but does not re-prove, the published boundary classification.

value.rationale: Geometric p-rank is a fundamental, deformation-relevant Jacobian invariant. For the complete newly classified natural boundary condition \(N\in\{2g,2g-1\}\) and \(p\mid N\), its possible values collapse to two extremes, with exact rank values at every family and a sharp moduli distinction between two curves with identical (p,N,g). The three nonrational tame quotients and their Cartier behavior explain the zero-rank cases. This is a motivated complete invariant classification, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice; it does not purport to give new p-rank techniques or full Newton polygons.
